title: SPONSORED: When one datacenter is no longer enough
gist: Sponsored interview teaser in which Cisco's Rakesh Chopra argues that power limits are forcing single AI training jobs to span multiple datacenters, requiring a new 'Scale-Across' routing approach with deep buffering, coherent optics and integrated silicon (Silicon One, Intelligent Collective Networking).

insights.claim: Power availability is becoming a hard physical constraint on AI cluster growth, pushing infrastructure teams to run a single training workload across multiple datacenters.
insights.speaker: David Gordon
insights.so_what: Power scarcity shifts value toward long-haul AI networking and multi-site orchestration vendors.
insights.quote: As clusters grow, power availability is becoming a hard physical constraint, forcing infrastructure teams to consider how a single training workload can operate across multiple data centres.

insights.claim: Traditional datacenter interconnect was built to move traffic between sites, whereas distributed AI training needs huge synchronous flows with minimal packet loss, where a stall in one part ripples across the whole job.
insights.speaker: David Gordon
insights.so_what: Creates a new DCI product category (scale-across) distinct from scale-up and scale-out networking.
insights.quote: If one part of the cluster stalls, the impact can ripple across the entire job.

insights.claim: Cisco argues the network is shifting from simple transport to an integral part of the compute system, with buffering, high-speed coherent optics and integrated silicon needed to make distant facilities behave like one deterministic machine.
insights.speaker: Rakesh Chopra
insights.so_what: Cisco is positioning Silicon One routing to capture AI multi-site spend against Nvidia/Broadcom/Arista networking.
